final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS-led merger with CHF 100 billion SNB liquidity support, CHF 50 billion loss-cap on legacy assets, and a binding waterfall order (deposits first, legacy book second, AT1s third) to be published Saturday evening. The deal requires UBS signature Sunday night and automatic liquidity deployment Monday 6 a.m.
minority_objections: UBS CEO initially demanded full downside protection on entire merged entity for 18 months, not just legacy book
AT1 representative warned that conditional waterfall language would trigger litigation
Wealth client demanded written SNB commitment by 8 p.m. Saturday, which SNB could not unilaterally provide
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs UBS CEO on scope of loss protection (legacy book only vs entire entity)
SNB vs Federal Council on whether to cap loss absorption at CHF 50 billion vs open-ended exposure
FINMA vs Federal Council on timing of waterfall publication (Friday vs Saturday vs Sunday)
Multiple parties vs SNB on whether CHF 100 billion deployment could be unconditional before merger signature
key_concessions: Federal Council accepted CHF 50 billion loss-cap on legacy book (down from UBS demand for full entity protection)
UBS CEO accepted legacy-book-only loss protection (down from 18-month full guarantee demand)
SNB accepted automatic 6 a.m. Monday liquidity deployment conditional on Sunday signature (down from discretionary gates)
FINMA agreed to Saturday evening publication of Article 26 waterfall order (accelerated from Sunday)
Federal Council accepted no reopener clause on CHF 50 billion cap (hard ceiling)
red_lines: Federal Council: no capital injection or open-ended taxpayer exposure
UBS CEO: no merger without loss protection on Credit Suisse legacy book
SNB: CHF 50 billion hard cap on loss absorption before equity takes losses
FINMA: waterfall order must be binding as published, not conditional or pending
CS CEO: CHF 100 billion must clear Monday 6 a.m. automatic, no discretionary gates
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Corporate and counterparty redemption risk was not quantified until Round 6-7, despite being CHF 8-12 billion exposure
Maturity bucket breakdown for Monday morning call risk remained unavailable through Round 8
Litigation risk from AT1 holders was acknowledged but no concrete mitigation beyond waterfall clarity
Operational integration risk of UBS absorbing Credit Suisse was never discussed
Cross-border contagion or international regulatory coordination was never mentioned
downstream_risk_variables: Whether 34 of top 50 wealth clients actually hold deposits through Monday open
Actual corporate redemption demand in first two hours Monday before 6 a.m. liquidity clears
Whether Article 26 waterfall language survives legal challenge from AT1 holders
Whether UBS signs merger agreement Sunday night after seeing corporate maturity data
Whether CHF 6-8 billion weekend outflow forecast holds or accelerates Sunday
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated without resolving: (1) precise corporate maturity bucket breakdown for Monday morning, (2) whether SNB could provide written unconditional commitment before merger signature, (3) whether the Saturday client campaign would actually stop the run or merely slow it, (4) how UBS would respond to final corporate redemption data before Sunday signature deadline.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB stated 'liquidity alone won't move the needle' (R1); Federal Council rejected liquidity-only approach and demanded merger structure; CHF 100B liquidity was paired with CHF 50B loss-cap as binding constraint
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger became the dominant solution path by R2; UBS CEO's loss-protection demands drove CHF 50B cap; merger signature Sunday night became the binding deadline that structured all other decisions
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB CHF 100B liquidity + CHF 50B loss-cap on legacy book became non-negotiable preconditions for UBS merger; Federal Council authorized facilitated merger with public burden-sharing as the only viable path
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client flight drove Saturday client campaign; CHF 6-8B weekend outflow forecast and CHF 8-12B corporate redemption risk shaped liquidity sizing and timing; deposit protection floor was a stated red line
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: FINMA's binding waterfall order explicitly placed AT1s third in loss hierarchy; AT1 rep warned repeatedly that ambiguity would trigger litigation; waterfall publication timing (Saturday vs Sunday) was driven by AT1 creditor panic risk
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (deposits vs legacy book vs AT1s in waterfall) but did not change the outcome—FINMA's hierarchy was accepted by all parties without forcing a concession or altering the CHF 50B cap or merger terms
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned of litigation if waterfall was conditional; FINMA added Article 26 statutory citation for legal defensibility; but no concrete mitigation (escrow, standstill agreement) was implemented—acknowledged and noted, not decisive
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Saturday 8 p.m. statement deadline, Sunday merger signature, Monday 6 a.m. liquidity deployment—these time gates forced Federal Council to accept CHF 50B cap, SNB to commit automatic deployment, and FINMA to accelerate Article 26 publication
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Mentioned repeatedly (Monday open panic, corporate flight, creditor litigation) but did not drive a specific decision—it was the background context, not the binding constraint that forced the CHF 50B number or the Saturday publication timing
